# Quarto-glossary

This extension provides shortcodes for [glossary](https://github.com/debruine/quarto-glossary) in quarto.


## Setup

### Installing

```sh
quarto install extension debruine/quarto-glossary
```

This will install the extension under the `_extensions` subdirectory. If you're using version control, you will want to check in this directory.


### Glossary file

You can store definitions in a YAML file. Use markdown to create paragraphs, links, and lists. Make sure each new line in a definition is indented two spaces (sorry YAML is a bit picky, but it's the best human-editable solution).

``` yaml
SESOI: |
  Smallest Effect Size of Interest: the smallest effect that is theoretically or practically meaningful

  See [Equivalence Testing for Psychological Research](https://doi.org/10.1177/2515245918770963) for a tutorial on methods for choosing an SESOI.
p-value: |
  The probability of the observed data, or more extreme data, if the null hypothesis is true. The lower the p-value, the higher the test statistic, and less likely it is to observe the data if the null hypothesis is true.
```

#### Grouping terms

Terms can be grouped under a heading by nesting them one level deep. Terms that
aren't under a group can sit alongside the groups.

``` yaml
html: |
  An ungrouped term.

Hypothesis testing:
  alpha: |
    The threshold chosen in Neyman-Pearson hypothesis testing...
  p-value: |
    The probability of the observed data...
```

Group names are not terms themselves, and grouping doesn't change how you use
a term: `{{{< glossary alpha >}}}` works whichever group `alpha` is in. Only one
level of grouping is supported.

#### Duplicate terms

Terms are looked up by name alone, so use each term name only once across all
groups. If a term is defined more than once with different wording, the first
definition in the file is used for popups and `definition=true`, and the extension
logs one warning for that term.

### Defaults

In the YAML header of your document, or the _quarto.yml file for your book or website, add the following defaults:

``` yaml
glossary:
  path: glossary.yml
  popup: click
```

Set `path` to the path to your glossary YAML file, and `popup` to "click", "hover", or "none". You can change these defaults for any individual inline glossary item.


## Examples

The simplest use starts with the word `glossary` and then the term to be defined. Click on the underlined word to see a pop-up definition.

`{{{< glossary power >}}}`

{{< glossary power >}}


### Display

No need to change if you're just using different case:

`{{{< glossary Power >}}}`

{{< glossary Power >}}

Use quotes if your term is more than one word.

`{{{< glossary "effect size" >}}}`

{{< glossary "effect size" >}}

Add a `display` argument if you want to display something different than the term:

`{{{< glossary alpha display="alpha criterion" >}}}`

{{< glossary alpha display="alpha criterion" >}}

### Popups 

The default is "click", which allows you to use styled html in the popup (see [Styles](#styles) below).

`{{{< glossary alpha popup="click" >}}}`

{{< glossary alpha popup="click" >}}

The "hover" option uses the web browser's built-in tooltip styles, so you can't use html in the definitions. However, you can now set the click event to open a link. 

`[{{{< glossary alpha popup="hover" >}}}](https://psyteachr.github.io/glossary/a#alpha)`

[{{< glossary alpha popup="hover" >}}](https://psyteachr.github.io/glossary/a#alpha)

Set popup to "none" to mark a term without a popup.

`{{{< glossary alpha popup="none" >}}}`

{{< glossary alpha popup="none" >}}

### Definitions

If you need to include a definition for a term that is not in the glossary file or is different from the one in the glossary file, you can set the `def` argument.

`{{{< glossary quarto def="An open-source scientific and technical publishing system" >}}}`

{{< glossary quarto def="An open-source scientific and technical publishing system" >}}

### Reuse a definition in the text

Set `definition=true` to insert a term's definition from the glossary file as
text, in any format. This keeps body text and glossary wording in step. A
definition with several paragraphs is joined into one run of text, and an unknown
term gives a warning and inserts nothing.

`{{{< glossary SESOI definition=true >}}}`

{{< glossary SESOI definition=true >}}

### PDF and other formats

Popups only work in HTML. In other formats, such as PDF and Word, the `nonhtml`
option controls how a glossary term appears:

| `nonhtml` | Result |
|---|---|
| `"text"` | The display text alone. |
| `"link"` | The display text, linked to the section given by the `link` option, for example a chapter of a book that holds the glossary table. |
| `"footnote"` | The display text, with the definition as a footnote on the term's first use in the document. |

The default is `"link"` if `link` is set, and `"text"` otherwise.

``` yaml
glossary:
  path: glossary.yml
  link: "#sec-glossary"
```

Both options can also be set on a single term. In HTML these examples are normal
popups; in PDF the first links to the Table section below, and the second gets a
footnote on its first use but not on its second.

`{{{< glossary power link="#table" >}}}`

{{< glossary power link="#table" >}}

`{{{< glossary p-value nonhtml="footnote" >}}}`

{{< glossary p-value nonhtml="footnote" >}}, and again: {{< glossary p-value nonhtml="footnote" >}}.

A term that isn't in the glossary file gets no footnote unless you give it a
`def`, which is then used for the note. In a book, each chapter is its own
document, so a term is footnoted once per chapter. An unrecognised value gives a
warning and uses the default.

### Table

Set `table=true` to get a table of every term in the glossary file. It works in
any format, keeps term case and Markdown formatting from the file, and lists terms
in the order they are written in the file. If the file is grouped, each group
gets a shaded band row naming it, with ungrouped terms first.

`{{{< glossary table=true >}}}`

{{< glossary table=true >}}

#### Only some groups

Use `groups` to include only some groups, as a comma-separated list. Names are
not case-sensitive, and an unknown name gives a warning. Terms that aren't under
any group are included when you don't use `groups`; to select them, or to mix
them with named groups, use the reserved name `ungrouped`.

`{{{< glossary table=true groups="effect sizes" >}}}`

{{< glossary table=true groups="effect sizes" >}}

`{{{< glossary table=true groups="ungrouped, hypothesis testing" >}}}`

{{< glossary table=true groups="ungrouped, hypothesis testing" >}}

Don't name a group "Ungrouped" in your glossary file: `groups="ungrouped"` would
select it together with the ungrouped terms, and the extension warns about it.

#### Layout

`layout` is `"grouped"` (the default, with a band per group), `"flat"`, which
lists the selected terms together with no bands, or `"list"`, which uses
definition lists instead of a table.

`{{{< glossary table=true layout="flat" groups="effect sizes, hypothesis testing" >}}}`

{{< glossary table=true layout="flat" groups="effect sizes, hypothesis testing" >}}

A definition list has one list per group, with the group name as a bold line
above it (ungrouped terms come first, with no label). The labels are not
headings, so they don't appear in the table of contents. It suits narrow pages
and outputs where a table doesn't fit well, and uses the `<dl>` element in HTML.

`{{{< glossary table=true layout="list" >}}}`

{{< glossary table=true layout="list" >}}

#### Order

`sort` is `"file"` (the default, the order written in the glossary file) or
`"alpha"`. Alphabetical sorting ignores case. In a grouped table the group names
are sorted first, then the terms within each group, with ungrouped terms staying
at the top. In a flat table all the terms are sorted together.

`{{{< glossary table=true sort="alpha" >}}}`

{{< glossary table=true sort="alpha" >}}

`layout` and `sort` can also be set as defaults under `glossary:` in your
`_quarto.yml`. An invalid value gives a warning and uses the default.

#### Table styling

In HTML the table uses Bootstrap's striped table style, and band rows have the
`glossary-group` class. In PDF the bands are shaded with the `glossarygroup`
colour, which needs xcolor's `table` option; without it, bands are unshaded.
